source_text: Paternus proconsul dixit: Non solum de episcopis , verum etiam de presbyteris mihi scribere dignati sunt. volo ergo scire ex te qui sint presbyteri qui in hac civitate consistunt. Cyprianus episcopus respondit: Legibus vestris bene atque utiliter censuistis delatores non esse. itaque detegi et deferri a me non possunt. in civitatibus autem suis invenientur. Paternus proconsul dixit: Ego hodie in hoc loco exquiro. Cyprianus dixit: Cum disciplina prohibeat ut quis se ultro offerat, et tuae quoque censurae hoc displiceat, nec offerre se ipsi possunt; sed a te exquisiti invenientur. Paternus proconsul dixit: A me invenientur. et adiecit: Praeceperunt etiam ne in aliquibus locis conciliabula fiant nec coemeteria ingrediantur. si quis itaque hoc tam salubre praeceptum non observaverit, capite plectetur. Cyprianus episcopus respondit: Fac quod tibi praeceptum est.
orientation: Paternus the governor continues questioning Cyprian at Carthage about the priests and the imperial orders against gatherings and cemeteries.
pass_a_gloss: Paternus the governor said: "They have deigned to write to me not only about bishops but also about priests. Therefore I want to know from you who are the priests who are present in this city." Cyprian the bishop answered: "By your laws you have voted well and usefully that there are to be no informers. And so they cannot be uncovered and handed over by me. But they will be found in their own cities." Paternus the governor said: "I am making inquiry today in this place." Cyprian said: "Since discipline forbids that anyone offer himself of his own accord, and this is also displeasing to your judgment, they cannot offer themselves; but when searched out by you they will be found." Paternus the governor said: "They will be found by me." And he added: "They have also ordered that gatherings not be held in any places nor cemeteries be entered. If anyone therefore will not have kept this so healthful order, he will be punished with death." Cyprian the bishop answered: "Do what has been ordered to you."

pass_b_english: Paternus the governor said: "They have seen fit to write to me not only about bishops but also about priests, so I want to learn from you who the priests are who live in this city." Cyprian the bishop replied: "Your own laws have wisely and usefully decreed that there are to be no informers, so they cannot be exposed and handed over by me. They will be found in their own cities."

Paternus the governor said: "I am asking my questions here today." Cyprian said: "Since our discipline forbids anyone to volunteer himself, and your own authority also disapproves of that, they cannot present themselves. But if you search them out, they will be found." Paternus the governor said: "They will be found by me." Then he added: "They have also ordered that there be no gatherings in any place and that the cemeteries not be entered, so if anyone fails to keep this most beneficial order, he will be punished with death." Cyprian the bishop replied: "Do what you have been ordered to do."
